title: Quentin and the Debt
premise: Rafael Montrose, a hostage negotiator haunted by the one call that ended in blood, receives a burner phone ringing with the voice of their dead mentor, Elias Vane—the man who trained them inside a covert network that manufactures negotiators and erases failures. The voice demands Rafael repay an old debt: one final job, brokering the release of a kidnapped auditor who has uncovered the network's ledger. As Rafael works the negotiation, they discover the 'hostage' is a stranger who shares their face, and that the debt was never money—it's Rafael's own erased identity, held as collateral since childhood. To save the auditor and themselves, Rafael must turn the network's own techniques against it, staging the ultimate negotiation with the man who made them. In the end, Rafael burns the training house to the ground, walks away from both names they've been given, and chooses love—Ana, the auditor—over the duty that was never truly theirs.
about_author: Rosalind Eriksen is a former crisis-line counselor who spent a decade listening to strangers talk each other back from the edge before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people whose professional calm conceals private fault lines, and she lives quietly on the Norwegian coast with two opinionated gulls.

chapters.title: The Number That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: Rafael Montrose, mid-negotiation in a Rotterdam bank siege, ends it flawlessly—then finds a burner phone in their coat pocket that they never put there. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: unease beneath professional polish; the past knocking at a door Rafael thought sealed.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Flashback woven through present: Rafael's recruitment at nineteen by Elias Vane into the Halcyon Group, a private firm that trains elite negotiators—and disappears its failures. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: nostalgia curdling into dread as memory contradicts official history.

chapters.title: A Voice from the Board
chapters.summary: The burner rings. Elias Vane—dead for six years, per every record Rafael can find—speaks calmly of an outstanding debt. He gives coordinates and a deadline: seventy-two hours. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: vertigo; grief weaponized against them.

chapters.title: The Auditor
chapters.summary: At the coordinates, Rafael intercepts Ana Reyes, a forensic auditor who fled after finding Halcyon's hidden ledger. She doesn't trust the negotiator sent to 'protect' her. POV: Ana. Emotional beat: wary friction; two liars circling for truth.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Halcyon's current handlers contact Rafael through official channels, ordering them to deliver Ana. Rafael realizes they're now the hostage-taker in someone else's script. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: the first open rebellion—small, deniable, irreversible.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Ana shows Rafael the ledger: decades of negotiated crises engineered to move markets and bury witnesses—including the failed call twenty years ago, staged so Rafael would carry the guilt. POV: Ana. Emotional beat: rage displacing shame; the failure wasn't theirs.

chapters.title: The Man with My Face
chapters.summary: The actual hostage surfaces: a young man named Tomas who looks unsettlingly like Rafael did at nineteen—a trainee, collateral, proof the program still runs. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: horror of recognition; inheritance as trap.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Holed up in Ana's safehouse, Rafael and Tomas run counter-surveillance while Ana decodes the ledger's final page. Trust forms over bad coffee and worse odds. POV: Ana. Emotional beat: tenderness growing in a siege mentality.

chapters.title: Handlers and Ghosts
chapters.summary: Halcyon escalates: Rafael's sister is followed, their apartment turned. Rafael feeds the handlers a false location, buying hours and making betrayal official. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: cold clarity—the cost of choosing sides is paid upfront.

chapters.title: Elias Explains the Debt
chapters.summary: Elias calls again and finally names the debt: Rafael's original identity, purchased and archived the day they were recruited. Repayment means surrendering Ana—or taking it back. POV: Elias (interleaved with Rafael). Emotional beat: seduction of the old master's logic meeting new refusal.

chapters.title: The Training House
chapters.summary: Following ledger coordinates, Rafael returns to the decommissioned facility where they were remade, finding it anything but empty—new recruits, new Tomas-figures. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: grief for the child who entered, fury for the ones still inside.

chapters.title: Counter-Negotiation
chapters.summary: Rafael proposes the unthinkable to Ana and Tomas: use Rafael's skills to negotiate with Halcyon itself—trading the ledger's public release for the recruits' freedom and Rafael's file. POV: Ana. Emotional beat: terrified faith; love choosing risk over safety.

chapters.title: Terms
chapters.summary: The exchange is set: a decommissioned ferry terminal, forty-eight hours, three lives for one archive. Halcyon agrees too easily. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into focus—too easy means a fourth variable.

chapters.title: The Fourth Variable
chapters.summary: Recon reveals Halcyon's plan: kill everyone at the exchange and blame Ana's 'terror cell,' closing the ledger forever. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into resolve; the trainee outgrows the curriculum.

chapters.title: Rewriting the Script
chapters.summary: The trio flips the ambush: Ana leaks a fragment of the ledger to force media presence, Tomas maps the shooters' positions, Rafael scripts a scene where Halcyon must perform innocence on camera. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: exhilaration of mastery turned homegrown.

chapters.title: Ferry Terminal
chapters.summary: The exchange begins under fog and floodlights. Rafael negotiates live with Halcyon's director while snipers wait and a journalist's stream runs. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: total control masking a hammering heart.

chapters.title: Elias Arrives
chapters.summary: Elias steps out of the director's shadow—he never died; he became the program. He offers Rafael the archive and a partnership: together they could own the machine. POV: Elias. Emotional beat: the last temptation, delivered with paternal warmth.

chapters.title: The Price of a Name
chapters.summary: Rafael refuses—not with a speech but with a question that unravels Elias before the cameras: what was your name before Halcyon? The director's composure cracks; the stream catches everything. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: catharsis; the weaponized empathy turned to truth.

chapters.title: Burn It Down
chapters.summary: Chaos: Halcyon's shooters fire anyway, Tomas takes a bullet shielding Ana, and Rafael triggers the failsafe—uploading the full ledger globally as sirens close in. POV: Ana. Emotional beat: terror and triumph braided together.

chapters.title: Aftermath Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Tomas survives; arrests ripple outward as governments scramble over the leaked ledger. Elias vanishes into custody of persons unknown—alive, unfinished. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: exhaustion without regret; some debts are settled, not closed.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Choice
chapters.summary: Rafael opens the sealed file containing their birth name and original family—and chooses not to reclaim it, telling Ana that who they became is who they are. They leave the file burning in a sink. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: quiet liberation; identity as choice, not inheritance.

chapters.title: The Phone That Stays Silent
chapters.summary: Months later, Rafael and Ana live unlisted and unremarkable until a new burner arrives in the mail. It rings once. Rafael lets it go to voicemail, then drops it in the harbor. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: peace earned, vigilance kept—love chosen daily over duty's ghost.
